host_validation.limitations: Complete native power shutdown/internal SoC shutdown/reinit and a bounded post-disable section execute against modeled CDS/parent-stop/probe/IRQ primitives. The native post-disable call now invokes production host preparation and qualified reclamation. SSR qualification results and later parent/probe operations remain models; no fake CDS callback performs retirement. Only explicit POST_DISABLED transient waits have a native module-suffix resume API; the native reinit callback performs one qualified module poll and the shared power tail before clearing the upper gate; pending/hard failures retain the transition; no independent worker/timer is installed; hard failures have no reset API; this is failure admission/propagation, not a complete recovery coordinator. Explicit native driver unload prefix now refuses globally retained private owners/journal before unload flags, bus unregister and component teardown. Full unload body, kernel module exit veto and module text references remain uncoordinated. Independent journal and upper power leases execute against a separate module-API ledger; successful module finish does not release the power lease before its tail ACK. Inherited scope reset discards synthetic retained references between cases and is not a production reset API. Linux loader/refcount concurrency and return-to-caller safety are not executed. IPCI remove preflight now refuses private lifetimes before sync unregister and preserves the transition; its actual callback, hardware disappearance and complete module unload remain uncoordinated and modeled here. Other bus remove paths are unchanged. Complete native adapter-reset function executes with modeled held-safe iterator, one active link per adapter, queue/scan/WMM/TWT/TDLS/stop primitives and VDEV references. No real SSR timing, kernel iterator concurrency, adapter-stop bodies or native parent teardown is certified by this reset fixture. Real helper C and extracted factory/rollback fragments with simulated HDD and synchronization. Complete native idle shutdown executes against modeled psoc synchronization, event and module-stop calls. SSR batch is a result/ownership model here; actual runtime batch, recovery policy and native callbacks are exercised by the separate existing runtime fixtures. The ordinary-idle coordinator executes production C against modeled runtime return values and synchronization; real native runtime destruction is covered separately, not end-to-end with this host here. This does not certify SSR/remove or prepared/UP recovery. Registry mutexes model spinlocks. Device and object-manager reference primitives are models; this validates host pin ownership and identity admission, not physical native parent deletion. Allocation pins do not preserve HDD, native components or firmware. Caller must retain and serialize complete parent lifetime across polls. The explicit handed-off SSR poll delegates qualification to the existing bridge and modeled batch here; actual batch policy/native cleanup have separate fixtures. Native SSR post-disable now reaches the qualified bridge; native reinit-triggered continuation is installed; independent retry scheduling and physical-remove coordination remain unconnected. This does not certify native kernel locking, teardown or radio validation.
